thread:
emily (CSE): heads up — during KiteHealth onboarding we saw a latency/quality regression after we flipped them to the int8 quantized variant yesterday. Ops-bot: alert triggered: model_latency_p95 > 300ms for customer=kitehealth :rotating_light:
diego (ML Eng): oh interesting — is that across all routes or just the shared/default one?
emily (CSE): mostly on the default route (shared-hosted). p50 stable (~85ms) but p95 spiked to ~380ms (baseline was ~150ms). cost dropped ~28% but answer-failure rate on our eval suite went 2.1% -> 4.7%.
ravina (AM): is the failure rate user-visible? any examples?
emily (CSE): a few hallucination/regression cases in the doc-summarization prompts we run as part of onboarding QA — sending examples to kitehealth (they saw one bad summary in staging).
matt (SRE): could be a KV-cache mismatch + batching for the int8 path. For some seq-lengths int8 kernels can regress latency under our current batching heuristics.
diego (ML Eng): agree. quick triage plan: 1) enable route-level canary to float16 compact model for 10% of requests, 2) enable prefix KV caching for high-hit routes, 3) rollback quant for the customer if canary shows regressions.
emily (CSE): plan sounds good. Raven/AE ok to schedule canary with KiteHealth? they prefer low-risk changes today.
ravina (AM): can do — I'll message their PM and confirm 10% canary window.
matt (SRE): ops snippet to create routing override (we'll run in staging first):
```yaml
route: "kitehealth-prod"
policy:
  prefer: dedicated
  fallbacks:
    - model: "redwood/gpt-compact-llm-v1-fp16"
      pct: 10
  cache:
    prefix_kv: true
    ttl_seconds: 300
```

matt (SRE): and CLI to kick off a canary:
```
rwctl rollout create --customer kitehealth --model redwood/gpt-compact-llm-v1-fp16 --route kitehealth-prod --pct 10 --notes "canary to mitigate int8 latency/quality regression"
```

diego (ML Eng): for monitoring, watch these: model_latency_p95, eval_fail_rate_on_promptset, prefix_kv_hit_rate. If eval_fail_rate > 3.5% or p95 > 250ms after 30m -> auto rollback to previous model.
ops-bot: will create an alert rule for those thresholds and post into #customer-success if triggered.
emily (CSE): action items: 1) ravina confirm with customer (ETA 30m), 2) diego create canary config and baseline metrics, 3) matt stage route override and alerts, 4) emily will send the regression examples to the ML team and the customer.
ravina (AM): confirming with PM now. :eyes:
diego (ML Eng): I'll prepare the eval harness and a quick perf run against the compact fp16 model. ETA 45m.
matt (SRE): staging rollout in ~15m if ravina gives the go.
emily (CSE): thanks team. if canary looks good we'll keep it for 24h before increasing or making permanent. If not, immediate rollback and schedule a deeper perf debug. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: alert created -> rule_id: ah-551234-01.
ravina (AM): customer approved 10% canary window for 2h. scheduling now.
emily (CSE): perfect — I'll update the onboarding ticket and the renewal-risk tracker (small blip but we flagged it early).
diego (ML Eng): noted — will post final numbers in this thread once the canary runs.
matt (SRE): leaving a note in runbook: if int8 causes p95 to exceed 300ms for specific seq-length buckets, prefer fp16 fallback.
emily (CSE): end state: try to keep cost gains where possible but not at the expense of user-visible quality or p95. we'll treat this as a proactive remediation and follow up in the renewal health check.
ravina (AM): great — thanks everyone.
emily (CSE): closing loop later with summary. :white_check_mark:
